name: package-lifecycle-scripts
description: Blocks fetch-exec class hooks and asks about other new ones when a change adds or edits code that runs at install or build time: npm install/prepare/pack scripts, gypfile without native sources, bin shadowing, unpinned git/URL deps; setup.py cmdclass and import-time calls, .pth imports, conftest, pyproject build hooks; build.rs and build-deps; go:generate; MSBuild Exec; gemspec, extconf, Podfile, Composer, Maven, Gradle exec. Judges file text, not what a hook runs. Friction, not a security boundary. [Session-enforced via PreToolUse and Stop hooks; needs git and a Python 3.11+. PreToolUse judges the file a tool call would write; Stop re-reads what the turn actually left on disk, so a file written through a shell heredoc is judged too. With no working Python the hook exits 2; without git, fail-open clients allow silently. A gate that cannot reach a decision refuses rather than allowing one it never judged. Enforcement at every commit and in CI still needs chock installed in the repo. Codex requires a one-time trust review per hook -- the plugin is ADVISORY until you approve its hook, and a plugin update voids that trust until re-approved.]
